messages:
IncidentBot: Paging severity=sev2 — console -> dataplane error spike for customer cluster 'acme-prod' starting ~2030001050. 90th latency > 3s and 5xx rate at 12%. Paging @oncall. Runbook: https://intra/redwood/runbooks/console-dataplane-mismatch :rotating_light:

Alex: saw it, I'm on. collecting logs now. tagging SRE. :wave:

Maya: I'm available to help with log pulls and timeline. which logs do you want first?

Jordan: quick hypothesis: config propagation lag or flag mismatch between control plane and dataplane agents. saw similar earlier with FLAG_X rollout.

Alex: agree. first step — confirm surface: is console UI showing older config than API? Maya can you run the two checks: (1) curl console /api/config and (2) curl dataplane /internal/config and diff.

Maya: running now.

Maya: output snippets:

```
# curl https://console.acme-prod.internal/api/config
{"feature_flags":{"new_routing":false,"batching_v2":true},"version":"2026-03-15T20:10:02Z"}
```

```
# curl http://dataplane.acme-prod.svc.internal:8080/internal/config
{"feature_flags":{"new_routing":true,"batching_v2":true},"version":"2026-03-15T20:09:57Z"}
```

Maya: diff: new_routing is true on dataplane, false on console. timestamps differ by ~5s.

Ryan: ping — that suggests control plane propagated config to dataplane but console cached older copy or didn't refresh. could be cache TTL or websocket event loss.

Alex: good. next: check event bus delivery for config update at ~2030001050. Jordan can you pull event logs from ctl-plane?

Jordan: grabbing from kafka, filtering key=config:update cluster=acme-prod since 2030001000. partial dump:

```
2030001048 INFO produced topic=config-updates key=acme-prod partition=4 offset=982374 payload={"flags":{"new_routing":true}}
2030001050 INFO consumer console-config-svc group=console-1 ack offset=982374
2030001052 ERROR consumer console-config-svc group=console-1 commit-failed offset=982374 cause=timeout
2030001053 INFO consumer console-config-svc group=console-1 retrying fetch
2030001056 INFO consumer console-config-svc group=console-1 ack offset=982374
```

Jordan: looks like console consumer had a transient commit failure for that offset and retried, which could explain the 5s lag.

Maya: also seeing increased 502s when console tried to apply policy change — UI calls to /v1/route resolved to older rules, causing dataplane to reject some requests.

Alex: customer impact estimate? any error rate mapped to customer-facing requests?

Maya: correlating — acme-prod error budget breach for 15m window, roughly 4% of requests failing higher-level route checks, some 502s surfaced to end users. not full outage but visible degradation.

IncidentBot: Incident notes updated. Current status: investigating. Severity still sev2.

Ryan: proposed mitigations: 1) force-console-config-refresh rollout (postfix consumer restart) 2) implement a NACK/retry backoff patch for console consumer to avoid commit-failed pauses 3) short-term: enable fallback routing on console to use latest dataplane view if mismatch detected. Which to run live?

Alex: do (1) now — restart console-config-svc consumer in canary mode across 2 pods. coordinate with on-call ops. I'll rollout canary to pod-1.

Jordan: executing restart on pod-1. command:

```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/console-config-svc -n acme-prod --pod=console-config-svc-1
```

Jordan: pod-1 restarted @2030002105. logs show consumer rejoined and caught up by 2030002110.

Maya: after pod-1 restart, checking console /api/config shows new_routing=true now. latency and 5xx rates have reduced ~60% in that canary segment. :thumbsup:

Alex: good. proceed to restart pod-2 with caution. I'll monitor.

IncidentBot: Note: scheduled customer notification drafted by ops — small blip, no SLA breach expected if trend continues.

Jordan: restarted pod-2 at 2030002402; all console consumers report acked offsets. global config timestamps aligned within 1s now.

Ryan: mitigation effective. lowering priority to containment. next steps for RCA: track root cause — why commit failed at 2030001052? hypotheses:
H1: transient network glitch between console consumer and kafka partition leader (intermittent)
H2: console consumer thread starvation under GC pause during config apply
H3: commit not idempotent due to offset commit race when rebalancing

Alex: collect GC logs from console-config-svc pods around 2030001040-2030001060 and network metrics between console and kafka leader. Jordan/Maya take those.

Maya: attaching GC snippet:

```
2030001039 INFO GC pause 120ms (young)
2030001045 INFO GC pause 450ms (full) heapBefore=1.2GB heapAfter=0.6GB
2030001051 INFO ThreadDump: consumer-thread blocked waiting on socket
```

Maya: looks like a full GC at 2030001045 might have contributed to delayed commit.

Jordan: network pings show 100ms spikes to kafka leader at 2030001050 but otherwise normal.

Alex: provisional root cause: GC-induced consumer pause caused commit timeout which led to delayed config application on console; dataplane had already received update. console then served stale config briefly causing route mismatch.

Ryan: remediation plan (short/medium):
- short: tune GC flags on console-config-svc to reduce full GCs; ensure consumer commit retries have jitter and exponential backoff (nev 2s windows)
- medium: add consumer-side watchdog to refresh state from dataplane if offsets lag beyond threshold
- long: change config propagation to include versioned push and explicit reconciliation checks between console and dataplane (and alert on >2s divergence)

Alex: create follow-up ticket and assign to eng-runtime for GC tuning + consumer fix. I've made ticket RUNTIME-4821. please add logs and timeline.

Maya: I've uploaded full kafka and GC logs to https://files.redwood/internal/incidents/2030001110/logs.zip and added timeline.csv

Jordan: I'll draft RCA note with chronology and hypothesis validation steps. cc @Ryan for remediation items.

Alex: handing off to Ryan for overnight watch at 22:30 UTC. Ryan, please continue monitoring and escalate if error rate creeps above 5% again. :eyes:

Ryan: taking over. will rotate watch and update status in #incidents. thanks team. :white_check_mark:

IncidentBot: Incident updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Tags: control-plane, dataplane, config-propagation, gc-pause.

Alex: closing thread from primary responder perspective, keeping open for RCA doc. last note: re-run smoke checks against acme-prod routing for 1h, and confirm no regression.

Ryan: will post update if anything changes.
